title: Sable and the Terminal
premise: Rafael Dunmore, a xenolinguist stranded on the forgotten colony of Sable, has spent years recording its slow decay in a language only he and the dying colonists speak. When the warship Meridian returns from deep space carrying crew members aged backward by relativistic time, they demand his recordings as evidence to justify restarting the war that orphaned Sable. Rafael must choose between loyalty to the colony that made him belong and the truth that his own translations were falsified to start it — and in delivering the corrected message, he condemns himself while freeing both worlds.
about_author: Rosalind Villalobos is a former field interpreter who spent a decade documenting endangered languages before turning to fiction. She writes about people caught between tongues, and lives where two rivers meet.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He records Maren Osei, the colony's oldest resident, as she speaks the last fluent sentences of Sable Creole, a language born of the first settlers' isolation. The colony is dying of neglect; supply ships stopped coming years ago. Rafael's quiet devotion to preserving what everyone else abandoned establishes his belonging here — and hints he no longer dreams in any human tongue. Emotional beat: tender melancholy, love for a fading world.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Meridian descends without warning, carrying crew who appear decades younger than their service records — time folded by deep-space transit. Their commander, Ilsa Reyes, recognizes Rafael as the linguist whose pre-war translation justified the blockade that doomed Sable. She demands his full archive to prove the enemy's guilt and reignite the war. Emotional beat: dread and vertigo; the past arriving physically younger than memory.

chapters.title: What the Record Actually Says
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Ilsa POVs. Reviewing the archive together, Ilsa discovers Rafael's original translation was altered under orders — the 'threat' was a plea for aid. Rafael confesses he knew and stayed silent, trading truth for the colony's fragile peace. As Meridian officers move to seize the recordings by force, Maren and the colonists form a human chain around the transmitter. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve; loyalty and truth at open war.

chapters.title: A Message in Both Directions
chapters.summary: Shared POV, converging. With the colony's power failing, Rafael broadcasts the true translation in Sable Creole and Standard simultaneously — a message that indicts both sides and offers the enemy's actual words: surrender terms sent years ago, never answered. The war hawks on Meridian are arrested by their own younger selves, aged backward and unburdened by old hatreds. Rafael stays on Sable to teach the creole to children not yet born into it. Emotional beat: costly absolution; grief transmuted into inheritance.
